title: A Way to Remember

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit wants to bring three things for a garden picnic. Trying to hold Zoe’s picture in his head leaves one thing behind; he invents a spoken check that helps him complete his own job.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Kit studies Zoe’s picture but brings only cups and a ball; trying to picture the missing item still leaves him uncertain.
storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit gives himself a three-part spoken reminder, checks the objects he already has and fetches the mat. He chooses his useful strategy rather than declaring one fixed learning type.

title: The Arrow Bookmark

storyBibleReview.storySpine: A magic bookmark slides along touching pencil arrows and stops at blank paper. Kit wants it to find his page, but opposing arrows trap it in a short back-and-forth until he corrects the route.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Kit restarts the bookmark without fixing the backward fifth arrow; it reaches the same local loop between arrows four and five.
storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit erases and redraws the backward arrow so the bookmark reaches the page. Zoe removes the route paper and closes the book with the now stationary bookmark inside.

setting: Classroom table. Explicit single magic rule: one plain red bookmark follows the direction of each pencil arrow beneath it and stops on blank paper. Six separate arrowheads share one continuous pencil shaft, with no blank gaps or overlapping heads. Arrows four and five initially point toward one another, making a short back-and-forth. It has no face, limbs or speech and cannot jump a blank gap. Ordinary erasing changes the route.

title: From Lava to Rock

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How does a moving lava flow become solid ground?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow a basaltic flow from hot moving lava through an outer crust, a still-hot interior and gradually thickening solid layers to rock retaining the flow shape.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Cooling changes melted rock into solid rock, and a dark solid surface can form long before the entire interior is cool.

scienceSources.title: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory: How do lava flows cool and how long does it take?
scienceSources.evidence: Explains early top/bottom crust formation, retention of heat by crust, progressive thickening and long solidification times in thick basalt flows. Solidification and cooling to ambient temperature are different; the final page does not claim all solid rock is cool to touch.

scienceSources.title: USGS: Why is the 2018 lava still so hot?
scienceSources.evidence: Observations show solid upper surfaces can cover very hot interiors; thicker flows can take years to decades to solidify and longer to cool completely. No single cooling time is asserted for every flow.

setting: One illustrative basaltic lava flow on a bare volcanic slope, inspired by observations at Kilauea rather than claiming a precise historic date. No people, buildings or animals near active lava. One low gray ridge at rear anchors the flow’s location; a geological cutaway is used only where specified.
props: One tongue-shaped basaltic lava flow
One low pre-existing gray ridge behind the flow

storyBibleReview.progression: Follow a frozen comet nearer the Sun as gas frees dust from its icy center; observe loose dust reflecting sunlight, then a fading tail farther away.

title: Gone or Still There?

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Can salt and sand be grouped by what happens when they are stirred into water?
storyBibleReview.progression: Compare small samples in equal water, let sand settle, then recover dissolved salt by unheated evaporation to show that invisible does not mean gone.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Both materials begin as grains, but a water test distinguishes dissolving from remaining as separate grains; the salt remains present even when it cannot be seen.

title: The Log Stays

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Why might leaving a fallen log beside a path help the animals underneath?
storyBibleReview.progression: Uncover a damp shaded patch with woodlice, connect their needs and feeding to the fallen wood, then restore the cover while removing actual litter from the path.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: A clear path and a retained small habitat can coexist; the log is shelter and food rather than disposable litter.

scienceSources.title: Woodland Trust: Common rough woodlouse
scienceSources.evidence: Describes dark/damp habitat, vulnerability to drying, seven leg-bearing segments and feeding on deadwood and leaf litter. Only those relevant claims are used; no reproductive details from this source are included.

scienceSources.title: Woodland Trust: Deadwood
scienceSources.evidence: Describes fallen and decaying wood as habitat, food and nutrient source. Also notes managers weigh location and safety; the manuscript deliberately places a small log beside an unobstructed path, not a dangerous standing tree.

setting: Shaded school garden edge beside a clear narrow path. One short partly decayed log, small enough for Kit to lift one end gently, lies outside the walking route beside a fern. Common rough woodlice, Porcellio scaber, beneath it; no handling of animals.
props: One short brown decaying log with moss on top and damp underside
One fern beside the log
Three visible gray woodlice, each with seven pairs of legs when exposed
Damp leaf fragments under log
One discarded blue wrapper on path
One small empty litter bag
